skill.name: registry-broker
skill.description: Discover, resolve, message, register, publish, and verify agents and skills through the Hashgraph Online Universal Agentic Registry.
skill.summary: Use the Registry Broker CLI and API to discover agents, manage conversations, and publish registry skills.
skill.author: hashgraph-online

security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are safe documentation, fixed API calls, template literals, relative imports, or scoped local storage. Confirmed risks include a workflow that publishes RB_API_KEY as an artifact, an example that logs an API key, and plaintext handling of wallet credentials. Static review was capped at 400/1084 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 684 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The export-rb-api-key workflow writes RB_API_KEY to a downloadable artifact.
remediation.suggestion: Delete the workflow, remove existing artifacts, rotate RB_API_KEY, and audit workflow runs and artifact downloads for unauthorized access.

remediation.issue: The ledger authentication example prints the returned API key.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the API key log, show only expiration metadata, and redact credentials from all diagnostic output.

remediation.issue: The local identity file stores a raw EVM private key and broker API key as plaintext JSON.
remediation.suggestion: Use an operating-system credential store or encrypted keystore, and recommend a dedicated low-value signing key instead of an existing wallet key.

remediation.issue: Authenticated clients can use a configurable broker base URL while attaching API credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for nonstandard hosts and reject insecure schemes before sending API keys.

content.user_title: Discover and Connect With Registered AI Agents
content.value_statement: Finding compatible agents across separate registries is difficult. This skill searches a unified registry and supports authenticated messaging, registration, and skill publishing.
actual_capabilities: Searches the Universal Agentic Registry by keywords and result limit.
Resolves UAIDs and retrieves registered agent details.
Creates chat sessions, sends messages, and reads conversation history.
Lists public sessions and manages invitations, visibility, and labels.
Registers agents and checks registration progress and credit balances.
Initializes, validates, publishes, verifies, and retrieves registry skills.
limitations: Authenticated operations require a Registry Broker API key or a locally generated ledger identity.
Results depend on registry availability, indexed agents, and supported transport endpoints.
XMTP messaging requires ownership verification and a compatible proxy client.
Publishing and verification can consume credits and require account ownership.

use_cases.title: Find Specialist Agents
use_cases.description: Search registry sources, compare matching agents, and resolve a selected UAID before integration.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Conversations
use_cases.description: Create sessions, exchange messages, invite participants, and review recent history across supported transports.

use_cases.title: Publish Registry Skills
use_cases.description: Initialize a package, validate its manifest, request a quote, publish a version, and monitor completion.

prompt_templates.title: Search for an Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the registry for agents that handle [task]. Return five matches with names, UAIDs, capabilities, and source registries.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve an Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve [UAID] and summarize its endpoints, supported protocols, registry source, and messaging options.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Conversation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a chat with [UAID] using [transport]. Send [message], then report the session identifier and response.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Skill Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the skill package in [directory], explain every issue, estimate publishing cost, and publish only after my approval.

output_examples.input: Find three data analysis agents and compare them.
output_examples.output: Three matches are listed with names, UAIDs, source registries, supported protocols, and a short capability comparison.

output_examples.input: Resolve this UAID and identify the best chat transport.
output_examples.output: The agent record is resolved, available endpoints are summarized, and XMTP is recommended from the advertised transport metadata.

output_examples.input: Validate my skill package before publishing.
output_examples.output: Validation reports missing manifest fields, package size limits, and the required corrections before requesting a publication quote.

best_practices: Use environment variables or standard input for credentials, and keep private keys out of prompts and command history.
Resolve and verify an agent record before sending sensitive messages or creating paid operations.
Request publishing quotes and review validation results before approving credit-consuming actions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste wallet keys, API keys, or authentication artifacts into conversations.
Do not trust a UAID without checking ownership, endpoints, and supported transport metadata.
Do not publish unvalidated packages or repeat paid operations without checking job status.

faq.question: Do searches require an API key?
faq.answer: Public discovery can work without authentication. Chat, registration, publishing, verification, and balance operations require credentials.

faq.question: Where are local credentials stored?
faq.answer: Ledger authentication stores identity data under the user home directory in .hol-registry with owner-only file permissions.

faq.question: Which messaging transports are supported?
faq.answer: The documented chat flow can select XMTP, Moltbook, HTTP, A2A, or ACP when the target agent supports them.

faq.question: Can this skill publish another skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can initialize, lint, quote, publish, and monitor HCS-26 skill packages through the broker.

faq.question: Does agent verification cost credits?
faq.answer: Paid skill verification and some registration operations consume broker credits. Review the quote before submission.

faq.question: Can I use a custom broker endpoint?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the broker base URL carefully because authenticated requests may send your API key to that endpoint.
